summary.text: Littlestone is a links on a stretch of land between Romney Marsh and the English Channel, opened in 1888 and shaped by Purves, Braid and MacKenzie.

setting.text: The course lies between the Romney Marsh and the English Channel, where sand dunes form natural, undulating ground.
The area is one of the driest places in Britain, so fairways are firm and fast.
Thick wild rough and classic deep pot bunkers demand accurate striking.
Top100golfcourses says it lacks the dune-laden terrain of its Kent neighbours but has plenty of movement, between holes 8 and 17 in particular.

history.text: The course opened in 1888 and was designed by William Laidlaw Purves, who also designed Royal St George's, and David Herd.
James Braid, then professional at Walton Heath, added bunkers to what was mostly a bunker-less course.
In 1924 the club asked Alister MacKenzie for ideas. He gave an extensive list of improvements, some made at once and some over the years.
The course has been virtually unchanged since MacKenzie, apart from tee relocation in 1997 for extra length.
Littlestone hosted the first ever Ladies' Championship in 1894.
Littlestone hosted the Ladies' Championship in 2002 and 2007, the British Ladies Amateur in 2005 and the 2011 English Girls Open Amateur Stroke Play.
The club also has a second course, The Warren.

trivia.text: A section of a Mulberry Harbour that did not make it across the Channel after D-Day in June 1944 is still visible from the 17th tee.
Top100golfcourses' 2015 Kent county ranking put the Championship course 4th in Kent, calling it largely eclipsed by its Open-venue neighbours.
The club describes itself as 'True Links Golf Since 1888'.

6.text: The par 3 6th is one of MacKenzie's contributions, along with the 17th.

12.text: The great fairway bunker on the 12th is credited to James Braid.

16.text: The array of cross bunkers on the 16th is credited to James Braid.

17.text: The par 3 17th is one of MacKenzie's contributions, and a piece of Mulberry Harbour is visible from its tee.

local.text: The club is at Littlestone, New Romney, on the Kent coast.
Top100golfcourses calls Royal St George's, Prince's and Royal Cinque Ports its links neighbours along the Kent coastline.
